html:
The Sobaipuri were an O'odham people of southern Arizona and northern Sonora, living in farming villages along the San Pedro and Santa Cruz rivers from the 1400s to the early 1800s. They were a branch of the O'odham, or Pima, of the region the Spanish called the Pimería Alta.

They irrigated fields of maize, beans and squash and traded widely. The Jesuit Eusebio Kino visited their villages from 1691 and founded missions among them; San Xavier del Bac, near Tucson, was built at a Sobaipuri village. They stood on the frontier against the Apache, and in 1762 the Spanish moved the San Pedro villages west to the Santa Cruz valley, where they merged with other O'odham. Their descendants live at San Xavier, part of the Tohono O'odham Nation.
